+### Runtime Config Environment Variables Follow the Type of Their Value

+An environment variable that overrides a [runtime config](/docs/guide/going-further/runtime-config#environment-variables) value is converted to the type of the value in `nuxt.config`, rather than guessed from its contents with `destr`. `NUXT_PORT=8080` is a number when `port` defaults to `3000`, and `NUXT_API_SECRET=4848e0` stays a string when `apiSecret` defaults to `''`.
+The server does not start if a variable cannot be converted (for example `NUXT_PORT=abc`), and reports [`NUXT_E8014`](/docs/errors/e8014).

+Runtime config values can also be [declared with a Standard Schema](/docs/guide/going-further/runtime-config#validating-with-a-schema), such as a Zod or ArkType schema, to set their type without a default or to make them required.
+1. Remove literal double quotes that were only there to keep a value a string, such as `NUXT_MY_VAR='"4848e0"'`. With a string default, the quotes are now part of the value.
+1. Make sure each default has the type you read it as. A value that defaults to `''` but is set to `NUXT_RETRIES=3` is now the string `'3'`. Give it a numeric default, or a schema:
+Plain values that default to `null` or `undefined` are replaced with an empty string, so they are set as strings too. A schema such as `z.number().nullable().default(null)` keeps its `null` default.

It is advised to use environment variables that match the structure of your `runtimeConfig` object.

-Environment variable values are automatically cast to their JavaScript type using [`destr`](https://github.com/unjs/destr). For example, `NUXT_MY_VAR=4848e0` becomes the number `4848`. To keep a value a string, the environment variable value itself must contain literal double quotes: in a `.env` file, write `NUXT_MY_VAR='"4848e0"'`; when setting the variable directly (in a shell, Dockerfile, or hosting dashboard), make sure the quotes are part of the value and not stripped by the shell (for example `NUXT_MY_VAR='"4848e0"' node .output/server/index.mjs`).
+Environment variable values are converted to the type of the value they replace:
+| Type of the default | Environment variable | Value |
+| object | `NUXT_MY_VAR='{"key":"value"}'` | `{ key: 'value' }`, merged over the default |

+A plain default of `null` or `undefined` is replaced with an empty string, so it is set as a string. To keep a `null` default and still coerce a variable to another type, use a schema such as `z.number().nullable().default(null)`.
+Nested keys of an object can also be set individually, such as `NUXT_SESSION_MAX_AGE` for `runtimeConfig.session.maxAge`. An empty variable is ignored for a key that cannot be an empty string.

+The server does not start if an environment variable cannot be converted (for example `NUXT_PORT=abc` for a numeric `port`). See [Validating With a Schema](#validating-with-a-schema) to declare the type of a value without giving it a default.
